name: Question 21
problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨4{e}^{2t},\,9{e}^{3t}⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(1,1)$ and has velocity $⟨2,4⟩$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$
worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector. To find the velocity vector, we first need to integrate the acceleration vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨4{e}^{2t},\,9{e}^{3t}⟩\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 4{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t,\int 9{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{2t}+{C}_{1},\,3{e}^{3t}+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(0)=⟨2,4⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0) & =⟨2{e}^{2(0)}+{C}_{1},\,3{e}^{3(0)}+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨2,4⟩ & =⟨2+{C}_{1},3+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=0$ and ${C}_{2}=1.$ Therefore, the velocity vector is

$$
v(t)=⟨2{e}^{2t},\,3{e}^{3t}+1⟩.
$$

We can compute the position vector by integrating the velocity vector.

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨2{e}^{2t},\,3{e}^{3t}+1⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 2{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t,\int (3{e}^{3t}+1)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{2t}+{C}_{3},\,{e}^{3t}+t+{C}_{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(0)=⟨1,1⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨{e}^{2(0)}+{C}_{3},\,{e}^{3(0)}+0+{C}_{4}⟩ \\ ⟨1,1⟩ & =⟨1+{C}_{3},\,1+{C}_{4}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{3}={C}_{4}=0.$ Therefore, the position of $P$ at time $t$ is

$$
r(t)=⟨{e}^{2t},\,{e}^{3t}+t⟩.
$$

Question 21
?

The acceleration a at time t of a particle P moving in the xy-plane is given by a(t)=⟨4e2t,9e3t⟩. Given that the particle is at the position (1,1) and has velocity ⟨2,4⟩ when t=0, calculate the position vector of P at time t.

a
 r(t)=⟨4e2t+t,9e3t⟩
b
 r(t)=⟨e2t+t2,e3t+t⟩
c
 r(t)=⟨2e2t,3e3t+t2⟩
d
r(t)=⟨e2t,e3t+t⟩
e
 r(t)=⟨2e2t+t,e3t+t⟩
Don't Know
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector. To find the velocity vector, we first need to integrate the acceleration vector. v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫⟨4e2t,9e3t⟩dt=⟨∫4e2tdt,∫9e3tdt⟩=⟨2e2t+C1,3e3t+C2⟩

We can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that v(0)=⟨2,4⟩. Substituting t=0, we get

v(0)=⟨2e2(0)+C1,3e3(0)+C2⟩⟨2,4⟩=⟨2+C1,3+C2⟩,

so we must have C1=0 and C2=1. Therefore, the velocity vector is

v(t)=⟨2e2t,3e3t+1⟩.

We can compute the position vector by integrating the velocity vector.

r(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫⟨2e2t,3e3t+1⟩dt=⟨∫2e2tdt,∫(3e3t+1)dt⟩=⟨e2t+C3,e3t+t+C4⟩

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that r(0)=⟨1,1⟩. Substituting t=0, we get

r(0)=⟨e2(0)+C3,e3(0)+0+C4⟩⟨1,1⟩=⟨1+C3,1+C4⟩,

so we must have C3=C4=0. Therefore, the position of P at time t is

r(t)=⟨e2t,e3t+t⟩.
